property_summary: When `assertGovernanceApproved` is called with a sender who has not transferred the flash governance asset but has a pending flash decision already expired (unlockTime < block.timestamp), the reference requires both conditions to be true (transfer AND pending decision expired) to proceed, while the buggy version uses OR, allowing governance approval without paying the asset.

A governance-approved caller can trigger assertGovernanceApproved by either transferring the flash governance asset OR having an expired pending decision, which is a critical logic error because the second version uses || instead of &&. The scenario uses a pending decision expiration to bypass the asset transfer requirement.

When a non-DAO user who is not governed calls assertGovernanceApproved, the reference requires BOTH a successful token transfer AND the pending flash decision unlock time to have passed (using &&), but the bug version uses ||, so it proceeds with just one condition true, causing an incorrect flash decision emission and state update that can be observed as the pending flash decision unlockTime being set to a non-zero value.

When a user calls assertGovernanceApproved and the flash transfer reverts (e.g., insufficient allowance), the reference version requires both transferFrom returning true AND unlockTime < block.timestamp to proceed, so it reverts with 'LIMBO: governance decision rejected.' The buggy version uses || instead of &&, so if pendingFlashDecision[target][sender].unlockTime < block.timestamp, the function proceeds even on transfer failure, allowing governance without paying.

After setting `flashGovernanceConfig.asset` to a token that `transferFrom` returns false, the reference version requires BOTH a sufficient allowance AND the unlock time condition; the buggy version (using `||`) allows governance when only the unlock time condition is satisfied, so another user can get a pending decision even though no tokens were transferred.

When non-emergency flash governance is attempted, the reference version requires time since last flash governance act to exceed epochSize, but the bug version incorrectly uses !emergency which allows emergency calls when time condition is not met.

Calling assertGovernanceApproved with emergency=true when the flash governance config asset is set, the user has approved enough tokens, and the last flash governance act is within the current epoch: the reference version allows the call (because it checks 'emergency || (block.timestamp - lastFlashGovernanceAct > epochSize)'), but the modified version breaks because it has '!emergency || ...' which requires emergency to be false, causing a revert.

When `assertGovernanceApproved` is called with `emergency = true` and the time since last flash governance act is less than the epoch size, the reference version allows the call (because the condition requires `emergency || (block.timestamp - lastFlashGovernanceAct > epochSize)`), but the modified version requires `!emergency || (block.timestamp - lastFlashGovernanceAct > epochSize)`, so the call reverts.

When emergency is true, the reference version requires block.timestamp - lastFlashGovernanceAct > epochSize, while the modified version inverts the logic to require !emergency (i.e., emergency must be false) for the same condition, causing the call to revert when it should pass.

When `assertGovernanceApproved` is called with `emergency = true`, the reference version requires the time since last flash governance act to exceed epoch size, while the buggy version inverts the logic (requires NOT emergency for the check), so the emergency action incorrectly succeeds when it should revert.

The reference version allows a flash governance action if the emergency flag is false and the epoch time has passed (OR condition), while the modified version incorrectly requires both emergency true and the epoch time passed (AND condition), causing a revert for a non-emergency flash governance call that should succeed.

In the reference version, assertGovernanceApproved allows a non-emergency flash governance action when the epoch time has elapsed (the condition uses '||'), whereas the buggy version incorrectly requires both 'emergency' and epoch elapsed ('&&'), causing a revert even in non-emergency which breaks the ability to execute flash governance without emergency.

When emergency is true, the reference version allows flash governance if epoch time has passed (OR condition), but the buggy version requires both emergency AND epoch time to pass (AND condition), so a call with emergency=true and insufficient epoch time succeeds in reference but fails in the buggy version.

When emergency is false, the reference version allows flash governance if epoch has elapsed, but the bug version requires emergency to be true (using && instead of ||), so calling assertGovernanceApproved with emergency=false reverts in the bug version but succeeds in the reference.

In the reference, a flash governance decision can be made when NOT emergency (i.e., emergency == false) as long as the epoch time has passed; in the buggy version, the require condition uses '&&' instead of '||', so it always requires emergency to be true, making the call revert for non-emergency even when epoch time has passed.
